rules: PRODUCTION_SPEC §1/§3/§9; flat LIGHT backgrounds; product cut out; 1–3 words on screen; a detailed 2-D object in every shot; watermark below content; logo end card; audio LOCKED. Length 45–55 s, HARD CAP 58 s. Draw no Motorola, Snapdragon or OnePlus logos (text names only). Fusion shown only as a generic phoneOutline with a text label. '53 hrs' always marked as Motorola's claim.
official_clips: none (Motorola posted no clips) — motion from kit objects + push-ins only
palette_for_this_video: paper main; mint for the reveal; sky for display numbers; blush for THE CATCH + WRECK; marigold accent for size/battery numbers
assets: assets_sources.md (A–H official motorola.in images ≥ 1600 px; R1–R6 official transparent cut-out renders)
new_objects: phoneOutline (generic unbranded slab phone, rounded corners, camera dot, `label` text under it, optional `size` in inches) — add to render/kit/OBJECTS.md. Reuse ruler, battery, counter, dialScale, sun, clockRing, hourglass, questionStamp, priceTag, scoreTable, chipDie, gauge, crossMark, arrowPointer, slider.

scenes.anchor: Motorola's small phone just got huge.
scenes.image: R3 (3/4 cut-out) starts small 35% height, scales up to 80%
scenes.object: ruler beside the phone grows 6.36 → 6.8 in (marigold tick)
scenes.note: frame 1 = poster A: phone + 'HUGE' readable instantly

scenes.image: A (hero, all 4 colours) centred, slow push-in
scenes.object: none extra; name label pill under image

scenes.anchor: The old Neo was compact. Now? It's six-point-eight inches.
scenes.object: phoneOutline (generic, label 'old Neo 6.36"') left, smaller; ruler between them 6.36" vs 6.8"

scenes.anchor: Get this. It hits fifty-two hundred nits!
scenes.object: sun icon brightens; dialScale needle to 5,200 nits

scenes.anchor: Motorola says fifty percent in twenty-seven minutes.
scenes.object: battery fills to 50 % while clockRing sweeps 27 min; small '45W' pill

scenes.anchor: And it claims up to fifty-three hours!
scenes.object: hourglass + counter 0 → 53 h; tiny 'Motorola claim' caption

scenes.anchor: Even with offers, you'll pay almost thirty-five thousand rupees.
scenes.object: priceTag swings in '₹34,999' with small 'with offers'

scenes.anchor: Motorola's own Edge seventy Fusion? It costs less.
scenes.object: phoneOutline (generic, label 'Edge 70 Fusion') right; priceTag '₹30,999' (mint) vs '₹34,999' (blush)
scenes.note: no Fusion product image (not in assets) — generic outline + text label only

scenes.anchor: It's got a newer chip, faster charging, and an ultrawide.
scenes.object: scoreTable 3 rows Neo vs Fusion: chip 7s Gen 3 vs 7s Gen 4 · 45W vs 68W · ultrawide ✗ vs ✓; rows tick in on each word

scenes.anchor: By our score? Fifty-one out of a hundred.
scenes.object: gauge 0 → 51/100, needle stops short of 55 line

scenes.anchor: It's a wreck. Want that battery? Your better pick is the Fusion.
Be honest. Would you pick battery or brains?
scenes.object: battery icon vs chipDie on a slider, cursor wobbles between them; logo end card after
scenes.note: loop back to scene 1 visually (small → big)
